PTMC JR. FINAL PROJECT
REPORT GRAPHIC ORGANIZER 
If lunar simulant is amended with organic fertilizers,
then the worm castings and compost will result in
the best plant growth compared to bone meal,
coffee grounds, and the lunar simulant control. This
is because worm castings and compost provide
necessary nutrients, whereas the bone meal, coffee
grounds, and lunar simulant lack the necessary
nutrients for sustained plant development.

Background/Reasoning
We chose the Plant the Moon Challenge because it
is more relevant for our preschool students since it
visible in the sky.
We chose the independent variables because my
students were curious about what helps plants
grow. These four organic fertilizers were the easiest
to obtain and teach the students about during the
project.
The dependent variables were the best variables for
the students to observe and measure. We taught
them how to measure with rulers and compared the
height growth using a graph of our data.
The students learned so much during this
project! The learned how to plant seeds, how
to measure water and height with a measuring
cup and ruler. They learned about plant growth
and what can help the plants grow more and
what can prevent the plants from growing.
The learned how to make comparisons and
work as a team.
They learned how to analyze graphs and plant
growth.
We are excited to continue to working with our
plants and watching them grow! We will be
planting more seeds in the future, too!

PTMC JR. FINAL PROJECT
REPORT GRAPHIC ORGANIZER 
Plant the Moon Challenge
Growth Chart Data
In analyzing the data, the students observed that the 3-in-1 Soil Starter
(Control) had the tallest growth. The plants with Worm Castings and
Compost added to the soil were the next two plants with the best
growth. 
After the final analysis of the data, the following plants in the photo are
the only ones still showing signs of growth.
It was fun to watch the bean plants grow taller
than our rulers, but I think it would have been
better to plant something that would produce
a fruit/vegetable before the end of the
experiment.
I would also like to use containers that would
allow our students to see the root systems.
Based on our data, our hypothesis was correct. The
compost and worm castings provided the best plant
growth when it was added to the lunar and Earth soil
mixture.
The coolest thing my students learned is that plants
can grow in lunar regolith. These plants did not
produce the highest growth, but it was fun to see
that the plants could grow in the lunar simulant
alone. They were very excited about the idea of
being able to grow plants on the moon! 
This challenge increased the students’ interest in
plant growth and the importance of plant growth in
our daily lives!
